thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: node/gpu-07 reported ephemeral-storage pressure -> eviction threshold reached for pods in namespace=redwood-serve. Auto-evict triggered. Suspected log spool + modelcache growth.
izzy_oncall: I'm on it. paging the GPU rotation oncall. visible error: kubelet eviction: "evicting pod due to nodefs.available below threshold". Which customers/pools hit?
alex_sre: seeing 5 pods evicted across node/gpu-07 and gpu-08, mostly modelcache-heavy replicas for model: /redwood/gpt-5-small. Restart loops on some.
maria_runtime: logs show modelcache corruption after restart, then CUDA init failures. excerpt: `E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:318] failed to allocate 1048576000 bytes: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` and then `runtime exit: coredump` on the container.
leah_support: Customer tickets: two premium customers reported increased 5xxs to /v1/generate ~10:12 UTC, duplicated requests and timeouts. No data exposure, but request latencies spiked to >10s.
izzy_oncall: immediate mitigation: cordon gpu-07, drain non-critical pods, reduce logging level for modelcache pods, and free up disk. Alex, can you confirm drain plan?
alex_sre: will drain with `kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` but deleting local-data will remove modelcache contents — that'll cause cold starts but prevents repeated eviction. suggest scaling down replicas for heavy models first to lower I/O.
maria_runtime: agree — scale down model replicas to 50% for affected modelset, and set `LOG_LEVEL=error` env for a short window to prevent log flood. Also patch the flush job to move old logs to persistent volume.
eng-qa: quick sanity check: how many restarts on a single pod? from kube: `RestartCount: 7   LastState: Terminated (OOMKilled)`
ops-bot: node/gpu-07 metrics snapshot: disk.available decreased from 12Gi -> 400Mi in 9m, inode exhaustion at 98%, logs dir `/var/log/redwood/modelcache` grew from 1Gi -> 11Gi.
izzy_oncall: Action list: 1) cordon node (done) 2) scale down replicas (maria) 3) kill runaway log writer processes (alex) 4) migrate modelcache to ram-backed tmp? not ideal. 5) open DRA to increase ephemeral storage requests for deployments.
alex_sre: I ran `kubectl scale --replicas=2 deployment/model-gpt5-small -n redwood-serve` and patched deploys to `resources.requests.ephemeral-storage=2Gi` for remaining pods. Also executed `pkill -f log-rotator` on gpu-07 (it was stuck in GC loop).
maria_runtime: triggered a model cache clear in place: `curl -X POST http://localhost:9001/modelcache/flush` on each restarted pod. That dropped disk usage on the node from 400Mi -> 2.4Gi as caches began re-populating in more controlled fashion.
leah_support: pinged customers: they will be informed about degraded latency window. SLO hit risk for 2 premium tenants; we should prepare credit calc if it extends >30m.
eng-qa: note: some containers after restart are hitting `cudaSetDevice` errors: `CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE` — likely because GPU assigned to process is in bad state after repeated crash. Rebooting node might fix.
izzy_oncall: we need to avoid node reboot unless necessary. Plan: schedule remaining pods onto other healthy gpu nodes, then drain and reboot gpu-07 as last resort. Jun, can infra spin capacity in dedicated pool?
devops_jun: spun up 2 warm spare nodes in dedicated pool, auto-join ok. Re-scheduled 4 affected pods onto gpu-02 and gpu-05. Deployment replicas now stable.
ops-bot: after reschedule: pod restarts dropped to 0 on new nodes, and `/v1/generate` 5xxs returned to baseline. However, one pod on gpu-08 still flapping with `OOMKilled` during model load.
alex_sre: for the flapping pod we increased `limits.memory` and added `LivenessProbe` tweak to allow longer startup. Also turned off `--log-very-verbose` flags for model-loader.
maria_runtime: observed kernel log during crash: ```kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (model-server) score 847 or sacrifice child
kernel: Killed process 23456 (model-server) total-vm:2048000kB, anon-rss:1024000kB```. Suggest adding guardrails to model-loader: pre-check available GPU memory and fallback to smaller quantized variant.
leah_support: Customer update posted to status.redwood.io: "Serving degradation for model gpt-5-small in some regions; mitigation in progress. No data loss."
izzy_oncall: Next steps (short term): 1) keep gpu-07 cordoned 2) move any remaining caches off node 3) add eviction alert threshold at 1Gi to early-detect log spikes 4) create hotfix to reduce modelcache prefetch concurrency. Medium term: increase ephemeral-storage requests defaults for model-serving, backfill persistent model cache for critical models, and add rotation job to push logs to persistent PV.
eng-qa: can we get a quick grep of log rotation failure? I found repeated stacktrace in rotator: `IOError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` when trying to rotate /var/log/redwood/modelcache/cache.log. It retried every 10s and appended to `cache.log.1` until both filled.
alex_sre: implemented temp workaround: mounted a 10Gi ephemeral volume onto `/var/log/redwood/modelcache` on gpu-07 to stop immediate evictions. This gives breathing room.
devops_jun: once we confirm stability I'll uncordon gpu-07, but recommend reboot after maintenance window to clear GPU state.
maria_runtime: added ticket to runtime backlog: "Model-loader should detect insufficient device memory and switch to quantized fallback; add configurable prefetch concurrency and disk write throttling."
leah_support: logged affected customers and initial impact window 10:11-10:34 UTC. Requested follow-up with engineering on credit eligibility if SLO breached.
izzy_oncall: closing loop for now: incident severity degraded to SEV2 (no full outage, partial performance hit). Keeping channel open for 30m for observation. Big thanks for quick actions. :tada:
ops-bot: NOTE: automated post-incident log saved to /var/log/incidents/1769456789.json (ops only).
eng-qa: reminder: include repro steps in postmortem: 1) simulate log rotator stuck 2) flood modelcache with large prefetch 3) check kubelet eviction behavior.
izzy_oncall: assigning owners: alex_sre (short-term fixes), maria_runtime (runtime hotfixes), devops_jun (node recovery + PV plan), eng-qa (postmortem test plan), leah_support (customer comms). Will start a retrospective doc and link to this thread.
leah_support: noted. drafting customer follow-up now.
izzy_oncall: thanks team. I'll update status once gpu-07 is back in rotation.
ops-bot: INCIDENT:ACK by izzy_oncall at 1769456792.
